conclusion: First-contact overhead repeats because each presigning session has a fresh Durable Object identity and each protocol request creates a new stub. No-op probes move the delay ahead of crypto and persistence. A fresh stub to the same warm object reproduces additional latency.
limits: The exact split among Cloudflare object allocation, route discovery and RPC connection setup is not exposed by these measurements. No durable first-contact optimization is implemented. Diagnostic probes add round trips and are not a product latency improvement.
method: Three existing hosted consecutive-signing scenarios. Random UUID parity selects direct or preflight arms. Probes use the same object and same stub; the third cohort additionally constructs a fresh stub using the same namespace, object name and options. All real requests retain storage durability and original authorization.
timing: Worker performance.now around awaited stub.fetch to response headers. DO wall and CPU from Cloudflare tail. Explicit storage.sync before returning real requests. syncClockMs includes frozen-clock effects and must not be labeled pure storage latency.
populations: workerPhases contains all retained Worker spans. phases and pairs include only correlations with both Worker and DO tail records. These have different sample counts and must not be interchanged.

source.routing: Object name hashes the presign session routing key; get_by_name constructs a stub for every call.
